title: Traffic governance and experiment patterns (sketch)
body:
PURPOSE: Working sketch for a lightweight traffic governance catalog that product, SRE, and solutions teams can use when planning canaries and A/Bs. Focus is cross-functional responsibilities, minimal required signals, and a short checklist to get a safe experiment running quickly.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Small, observable canaries first. Start with health + correctness + business signal.
- Define ownership and a single responder per signal.
- Use conservative slice sizing (0.1% / 1% / 5% tiers) with automatic rollback thresholds.
- Keep hypothesis and primary metric short; everything else is supporting signals.

1) Experiment types and when to use them
- Rapid validation (low risk): feature flag behind small traffic slice; focus on functional correctness and latency.
- Quality/regression check (medium risk): canary to detect model regressions or degraded outputs; include both automatic unit tests and human-in-the-loop sampling.
- Business impact A/B (higher risk): run larger slices with holdout; tie to revenue/usage metric and plan ramp cadence.

2) Minimal cross-functional template (one pager to attach to tickets)
- Name: short descriptive token
- Hypothesis: one sentence (what we expect to change)
- Primary metric (+ expected direction and effect size)
- Experiment type: quick/quality/business
- Initial slice size: (pick tier)
- Duration: min 24h, recommended 72h for behavioral metrics
- Owner: product owner + SRE on-call alias
- Rollback condition(s): clear thresholds, e.g., error rate +0.5pp, p95 latency +50ms, primary metric drop >3% absolute
- Monitoring dash link and sampling query

3) Traffic slice tiers (recommended)
- Tier A (smoke): 0.1% — used for code and basic correctness. Short run (1–6h). Abort on any functional failure.
- Tier B (validation): 1% — used for model/content regressions and early business signals. Run >24h, require manual sign-off to advance.
- Tier C (ramp): 5–20% — used for stronger A/B tests. Requires pre-approved rollout plan and k-anonymized logs if needed for privacy.

4) Guardrails and automatic controls
- Health guardrail (platform): 5xx spike +20% over baseline OR latency p95 +60% triggers immediate traffic cut to fallback.
- Correctness guardrail (product): automated quality checks fail on 3 consecutive batch samples -> pause.
- Business guardrail (GTM/product): primary metric deviation beyond predefined window triggers alert to owners and rollback recommendation.
- Circuit breaker behavior: traffic halves on first trigger, drops to 0 if repeated within 15m.

5) Signals to monitor (must-have list)
- Infra: 5xx rate, 4xx rate, p50/p95 latency, GPU memory pressure, queue depth
- Model/product: response schema errors, function-calling failure rate, hallucination proxy (failed fact-checking rules), token growth anomalies
- Business: conversion rate, click-through, sessions per user, retention window (24h, 7d), revenue per session if applicable
- Quality sampling: daily random sample of 100 responses evaluated by rubric for safety/accuracy

6) Roles & RACI (short)
- Product: defines hypothesis, primary metric, success criteria, and business rollback policy
- SRE/Platform: configures traffic split, implements circuit breaker and latency-based policies, guarantees rollback automation
- Solutions/SEs: manage customer communication for Dedicated/Private customers if affected
- Data/Analytics: provide pre- and post-experiment queries and short-run analysis (24h and 72h)
- Responsible owner: person listed on the one-pager; Pager duty alias is the emergency responder

7) Communication plan (before / during / after)
- Before: short Slack thread in #console-rollouts, attach one-pager and dashboard link; tag SRE and analytics owners
- During: status updates every 6h for Tier B or higher, immediate alert to #incidents if guardrail tripped
- After: 72h write-up with outcome, metric windows, and next action (rollback, full rollout, iterate)

8) Quick checklist for runbook automation (ops handover)
- Create experiment ticket with template and link to dashboard
- Add circuit-breaker config to infra repo and point it at the test slice
- Create sampling job for quality checks and assign raters
- Confirm SLOs and rejection thresholds in the dashboard
- Dry-run the rollback (simulate cut in staging)

9) Example rollback thresholds (suggested defaults)
- 5xx rate increase >0.5 percentage points vs baseline (5m sliding window)
- p95 latency +50ms vs baseline for two consecutive 5m windows
- Primary business metric decline >2% absolute in 24h comparing similar traffic cohort

10) Open questions / things to iterate on
- How to standardize the hallucination proxy across models? (Ravi to draft sampling rubric)
- Should we require data-team sign-off for experiments touching billing metrics? (pending legal review)
- Automated graduated rollback vs abrupt kill: tradeoffs for UX vs safety (SRE preference leans to graduated)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Build a lightweight experiment tag in the console to map requests to experiment id for easier slicing and post-hoc analysis.
- Template PR for infra that wires circuit-breaker defaults and makes them configurable per-experiment.
- Add a one-click mute for telemetry noise when testing tiny slices (to avoid paging on 0.1% jitter).

References and links (work-in-progress):
- Slack: #console-rollouts and #infra-alerts
- Confluence: experiment-governance-v2 (draft)
- Jira: INF-4021 (circuit breaker improvements)

---
Informal, sketchy — intended as a conversation starter for the cross-functional kickoff. If this looks useful, I'll convert the template into the one-pager and a small console flow for quick creation.
